RCT comparing two anaesthetic drug regimens (different fentanyl infusion techniques with ketamine and droperidol). Study measures explicit memory and dreams during anesthesia, which relates to awareness. Meets inclusion criteria as an RCT of anaesthetic regimens.

Prospective observational study analyzing pharmacodynamic interaction between drugs on BIS values. Not an RCT testing anaesthetic interventions for awareness prevention. Objective is to characterize drug interaction, not evaluate efficacy of interventions.

Study develops and validates EEG/AEP models for detecting consciousness vs unconsciousness. While it compares with BIS, it is not an RCT testing anaesthetic interventions for awareness prevention. It is a methodological study.
Study conducted in nine healthy volunteers. Selection criteria explicitly exclude volunteer studies. Does not meet inclusion criteria.
Two-phase study (control phase then BIS phase) without randomization. Not an RCT. While it uses BIS monitoring, the study design does not meet the RCT requirement.

RCT testing esmolol and nicardipine for hemodynamic stability during anesthesia. These are not anaesthetic regimens or depth monitors for awareness prevention. Primary outcomes are recovery times and hemodynamic parameters, not awareness.
Observational study reporting incidence of awareness from 19,575 patients. No intervention tested. Not an RCT of anaesthetic interventions.

Randomized prospective study comparing two anaesthetic regimens (propofol-remifentanil vs sevoflurane-N2O). Anaesthetic depth monitored by BIS. Meets inclusion criteria as an RCT of anaesthetic drug regimens.
RCT comparing BIS-guided closed-loop propofol titration vs manual control. Tests anaesthetic depth monitor (BIS) for maintaining appropriate anaesthetic depth. Meets inclusion criteria.

Study compares etomidate to thiopentone sodium as induction agents. Abstract does not clearly state randomization. Mentions 'further large series' suggesting possible observational component. Unclear study design prevents confident inclusion.
Software documentation for R meta-analysis package. Not a clinical study. Completely irrelevant to the review topic.
Comparative study of Narcotrend vs BIS monitors. Not an RCT testing interventions for awareness prevention. Study compares monitor performance rather than testing efficacy of interventions.

Randomized study comparing remifentanil-based anaesthesia with desflurane/sevoflurane vs conventional alfentanil-desflurane technique. Reports 'no awareness occurred'. Meets inclusion criteria as RCT of anaesthetic regimens.

RCT comparing anaesthetic techniques but primary outcomes are cortisol and catecholamine levels (stress response), not awareness. Diazepam given to prevent awareness but awareness not measured as outcome. Does not meet review objective.
RCT comparing propofol/epidural vs propofol/epidural/nitrous oxide. Title explicitly mentions 'postoperative awareness' as outcome. Meets inclusion criteria as RCT of anaesthetic regimens.
RCT comparing 3% vs 4.5% desflurane concentrations with BIS monitoring to prevent awareness in caesarean section. Background states purpose is 'to prevent awareness'. Meets inclusion criteria.
Prospective case study/interview study of 11,785 patients. No intervention tested. Observational study of awareness incidence and sequelae. Not an RCT.
Case series reporting 14 representative cases of awareness. No intervention tested. Descriptive report only. Not an RCT.

RCT comparing tramadol vs morphine administered during wound closure. Abstract mentions 'tramadol may cause awareness and EEG activation during anaesthesia' and confirms tramadol did not antagonize hypnotic effects. Tests anaesthetic adjunct affecting awareness risk.
